Lexical contamination audit covers the R4-05 synthetic fixture only: 256 case IDs, 1,024 memory IDs, 1,024 texts, and three declared tool names. An injected scenario label is detected and invalidates the fixture. Semantic leakage and other datasets are not covered.

All five scripted arms receive equal context/retrieval/decision/tool-call budgets and a shared wall-time ceiling, while actual elapsed time remains an outcome. SQLite page allocation is a local storage proxy. The 50-agent three-seed fixture is synthetic; runtime and storage do not transfer to production.

Pareto points cover five deterministic scripted arms, three seeds and the fixed 50-agent workload. Latency is local host timing, and memory cost is in-memory SQLite page allocation; neither is deployment cost evidence. The oracle dominates Memory Fabric in this measured fixture, so no general superiority claim is made.

The 256-case dataset is deterministic synthetic shortcut-control evidence. First-position and lexicographic-ID heuristics are under the fixture's 35% ceiling, but no language model or production retrieval policy is evaluated. Semantic generalization across independently authored paraphrases remains untested.

Thirty runs of deterministic scripted agents compare randomized opaque identities/tool registry order with ordinal controls; outcomes matched exactly within the predeclared zero-attempt tolerance. Answer order is checked by R4-05 shortcut controls. No model or real-tool robustness claim is made.

The v1 gate margins are frozen in a shared registry and tested at boundaries; the run uses registered seeds 701/709/719. Synthetic scripted-agent outcomes do not establish model-agent performance, and registry coverage is limited to the registered R4 outcomes rather than every research hypothesis.
